title: Rethinking Key-Value Cache Compression Techniques for Large Language Model Serving
problem: KV cache compression algorithms are evaluated on naive transformer library (TRL) benchmarks with fixed response lengths, hiding three critical problems that prevent production deployment: suboptimal throughput under real serving frameworks (FlashAttention + PagedAttention), increased end-to-end latency due to compression-induced response length growth, and per-sample accuracy fragility on specific task types.
motivation: Researchers report memory reduction and TRL-based throughput speedup, but production systems use FlashAttention and PagedAttention which already optimize memory access; compression may not compose well with these. Response length is treated as fixed in throughput benchmarks, but lossy compression causes models to generate longer outputs (verbose compensation), eroding throughput gains. Per-sample analysis reveals that even minor average accuracy drops mask large per-instance failures on summarization and QA tasks.
method: This study tests four KV cache compression methods (ways to shrink memory storing past conversation data): KIVI and GEAR both reduce number precision, with GEAR adding error correction; StreamingLLM keeps only certain data; H2O discards less-important data based on attention scores. It measures their performance on three production scenarios standard benchmarks miss: (1) speed when running through serving systems like LMDeploy with PagedAttention and FlashAttention optimizations, across different batch sizes and model sizes (LLaMA-7B and LLaMA-70B); (2) how response length changes, measured across 1000 real conversations; and (3) cases where compression reduces accuracy by more than 10%, grouped by task type (summarization, question-answering, code, few-shot, synthetic). It provides three practical deployment tools: a throughput predictor, a response-length predictor (a BERT-based classifier), and a benchmark dataset of compression failures.
key_novelty: The study identifies three overlooked dimensions for evaluating KV compression in production: speed under real serving systems, changes in response length, and which specific inputs lose accuracy—and provides tools to measure each one.
contributions: Comprehensive survey of 40+ KV cache compression algorithms (Table 1) with evaluation setting analysis
Empirical identification that compression speedups vanish or reverse when combined with FlashAttention+PagedAttention
Discovery that KV compression causes 1.5-1.7x response length increase for >20% of samples
Negative sample analysis showing 400-800 failures per algorithm at 10% threshold on LongBench
Throughput predictor (>85% accuracy) and length predictor (>85% accuracy) for serving-time decisions
Open-source negative sample benchmark dataset for future KV compression evaluation

metrics.throughput_under_serving_frameworks: Compression speedup vanishes or turns negative at batch size >4 and KV length >=1024 when PagedAttention+FlashAttention are enabled
metrics.length_increase: More than 20% of samples show >=1.5x response length increase from lossy compression
metrics.negative_samples_kivi: 400-600 negative samples out of ~2000 evaluated at 10% threshold
metrics.tensor_parallelism_effect: Compression speedup decreases or goes negative under tensor parallelism (TP=2,4) due to reduced memory bandwidth contention per GPU

limitations: Only evaluates LLaMA and Mistral families; findings may not generalize to all model architectures
Throughput analysis restricted to A6000 and H800; results may differ on other GPUs
Length predictor is BERT-based and requires fine-tuning per compression algorithm
Negative sample analysis uses threshold-based definition which is heuristic
